summary: East India Companies is a mid-weight economic game where players race ships to trading regions, sell goods for profit, and grow their fortune partly by investing in shares of their own or rivals' companies. It plays as an accessible on-ramp to heavier stock/pick-up-and-deliver games, with tension coming from speed to market and fluctuating prices rather than direct conflict.
praised: Accessible, clean rules make it a good "gateway" to heavier economic/18XX-style games
Loading/Selling loop with shifting profit margins stays engaging and "fresh" across multiple plays
Pick-up-and-deliver ship placement creates real tension and drama around who gets to a region first
Clever mix of stock investment and buy/sell tactics rewards reading the market
criticised: Thematically odd that buying shares in a rival's company pays no money to that player
Only one language's player aid included, and new players often misjudge early stock investments before they understand the economy
Some players find rounds start to feel repetitive/samey over a full game
Best experienced at higher player counts (4) — with fewer players the market tension and competition soften noticeably
Some forum discussion criticizes the colonial-trade theme as glossing over real-world exploitation

interaction.detail: Players share regional markets where the fastest ship to arrive gets first pick of available goods, so speed and timing directly affect what's left for others. Players can also buy shares in each other's companies, tying part of everyone's fortune to rivals' fluctuating success, though each player still manages their own ships, cash, and holdings on a mostly individual board.

scoring.why: Final standing is determined by total wealth—cash on hand plus the value of company and personal shares—rather than a points track.
scoring.how_you_win: Trade goods profitably, invest in your own and rival companies' shares, and time the fluctuating market so your combined cash and share value is highest when the game ends.
